chunks.arabic_text: ٢٠ - مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، الْهَمْدَانِيُّ، أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ.

translations.en: 20 – Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, al-Hamdānī, Abū Jaʿfar.

chunks.arabic_text: كَانَتْ لِأَبِيهِ وَصْلَةٌ بِأَبِي الْحَسَنِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ). وَحَدِيثُهُ يُعْرَفُ وَيُنْكَرُ. وَيَرْوِي عَنِ الضُّعَفَاءِ كَثِيرًا، وَيَعْتَمِدُ الْمَرَاسِيلَ.

translations.en: His father had a connection to Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him). His ḥadīth are recognized and denied. He narrates from the weak narrators a lot, and relies on the mursal narrations.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* highlights the nuanced evaluation of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Hamdānī, whose familial link to Imam al-Rida (AS) did not guarantee his narrational reliability. The text underscores a key methodological concern in Shia hadith criticism: the prevalence of 'mursal' (disconnected) chains and reliance on weaker transmitters, which often led to his reports being both accepted and rejected by scholars.
en.seo_question: What is the biographical status and reliability of Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm al-Hamdānī in Shia hadith sciences?
